goal: Each house crawl lane runs at least at its share of the 250 GB GeoNode month on prod, read the way the crawler Throughput dashboard on obs.virev.ai shows it, and Instagram re-reads meet the owner's goal on Crawler guy's board item p8. The duty moved from Crawler VP's d9 to Crawler guy's d8 on 11-24 (owner, t9), and its old lines (Instagram 10,000 profiles a minute, TikTok Shop 99.5% weekly coverage, Meta every due walk in 7 days) left that day, because 10,000 profiles a minute alone is about 20.8 TB a month. The split, from the 11-24 lane pricing page (prod crawler.proxy_wire_reads at the 11-01 to 11-09 pace) with three later corrections: staging is about 13 GB a month after the Bing one-warm-session change 7b4031931c and the media_refresh pause 247e77103a; prod paid and upkeep reads are about 91 GB after the Bing cut and the 7-day doc-ids sweep c637e1856c, and that 91 GB holds the demo Watchlist's 30 GB of Instagram walks and 24 GB of collab walks but no census read, because the pricing page counts the census lane as house with a paid part of 0; the demo Watchlist costs 93 to 101 GB a month with its own engage, anon and census reads (Search product, misc.'s brand-monitor-cost page of 11-24), so its 54 GB of walks leave the 91 GB and its high end comes in once. 250 GB less 13 GB less (91 - 54) GB less 101 GB leaves 99 GB for prod house lanes, the low end of 99 to 107, which ran 65,354 GB a month, so every house lane keeps 99 / 65,354 of its old pace. Census ran 23,979 GB, so it gets 36.3 GB; TikTok Shop 4,010 GB, so 6.07 GB; Meta Ads 1,583 GB, so 2.40 GB. GeoNode counts 1.1375 bytes per wire byte. One ok census profile read is 42,296 wire bytes (2.06 TB over 48.7M ok census jobs, 11-06 to 11-09), 48,112 counted; one ok TikTok Shop product row is 76,334 wire (974 GB over 12.8M rows), 86,830 counted; one Meta advertiser walk is 12,411 wire (16.4 GB a day over 1.32M walks a day), 14,118 counted. A month is 43,200 minutes, so the lines are 36.3 GB / 48,112 B / 43,200 = 17.5 Instagram house census reads a minute, 6.07 GB / 86,830 B / 43,200 = 1.6 TikTok Shop good products a minute, and 2.40 GB / 14,118 B / 43,200 = 3.9 Meta advertiser walks a minute. Each row counts house reads only. Instagram counts ok census jobs with product = 0 in crawler.instagram_census_reads, the unit the 48,112 B price is per; a product read (a user's request, a Watchlist sweep or a brand crawl, and the post and post count jobs behind it, marked since auto-sns-agent 2fb1ca110) is paid work, so the line leaves it out and the run detail shows it, because on 11-24 the line counted every instagram_account_snapshots row and the demo Watchlist's census reads, about 19.7 a minute, passed it alone. TikTok Shop counts its ok product rows, and only the house walker writes them with no paid origin bound; both read the slowest rolling hour of the last 6 h with the 5-minute slots under prod's deploy lock left out (deploy downtime is p6's number). Meta Ads reads advertiser walks finished over 24 h, which only the house scheduler's walks add to, since a paid live read counts no finish. TikTok Shop's 7-day coverage and Meta's walks due now stay in the run detail. Instagram re-reads read their goal from p8 at run time (owner 10-26 "1k+ every month, 10K+ every week" and "under 1k also monthly"): at most that share of read accounts with 10,000+ followers past 7 days, and of the rest past 30 days, two rows from page samples of instagram_census. At 48,112 B a read they cost about 21 TB a month (12.1M 10k+ accounts weekly and 386M others monthly), 84 times the whole plan, a decision for the owner. The census Postgres writer (Crawler VP's p895) is one more row: its worst lag over 24 h, in the 5-minute slots where census reads, house and paid, since the writer takes both, run at the Instagram line or more outside deploys, stays at most 5,000 records. The supporting metrics keep the rest of the owner's 10-19 duties: no Instagram queue backlogs, which is a 30-minute low over 80k records or growth over 6 h (p827), and every panel on the crawler dashboards draws. The lines are floors on each lane's share, and Search product, misc.'s d4 watches the month's total. GeoNode Mbps left this duty on 11-24 with the old lines. The census job failure share is reported in the run detail against the owner's 40 to 70% band, and a rise past it is an alert rule's job. The lines are floors, so a lane that burns the plan never misses them; the fourth metric reads that upper side (owner, #1124-cost-management p52 and p54 on 11-28, after a PostHog sync cost up to $80 a day for 11 days while a daily check read a number it could not judge). It counts every prod crawl lane of crawler.proxy_wire_reads and every product-read caller of product.usage_events (an org and its action, every action that booked wire bytes) whose wire GB in the last 24 h passed 2 times its median over the 7 days before and added 0.7 GB or more; a day with no read is a stop, such as the GeoNode lapse, and the median skips it. The 2x line comes from a replay of the d8 run times from 11-24 to 11-28: normal groups of 0.3 GB or more read at most 1.18x, while the 11-24 07:00 to 09:00Z census burst, the 11-25 websearch burst (2.41x on the api lane, a new caller at 1.2 GB), CRM's 11-27 pace (a new caller at 1.0 to 2.9 GB) and the demo Watchlist's 5.8 GB first sweep after the lapse all pass it. The 0.7 GB line is the smallest one-off room the 11-26 split of the GeoNode month left a day. A lane or caller the read leaves out or cannot read counts as not measured, never as fine.

metrics.label: Crawl lanes under their share of the 250 GB plan, and p8 re-read rows missed
Instagram queues that backlog: over 80k at their 30-minute low, or grown over 6 h
Panels on the crawler dashboards on obs.virev.ai that show an error or No data
Prod crawl lanes and product-read callers whose wire GB in 24 h passed 2 times their 7-day median and added 0.7 GB or more

onMiss: For each missed metric, start or steer one live fix job this run, and keep it until the metric is met again. A live job that already owns the cause gets the numbers by message. Otherwise start one and put its fix step under the matching goal with duty "<id>/<metric>": the Instagram re-read rows go under p8, every other row under p6. throughput_goals_missed: the goal lines name each platform's rate against its goal; for each missed one find what stopped or slowed that crawl (a pause, a deploy, a hold, the proxy, a crashed role, a writer, a cadence control such as weekly_days or small_recheck_days) from the Throughput dashboard and logs, and get it back with a code or config fix through the crawler ops train, or a control write through /ops/controls with a measured reason. Bring a lane up to its plan line and no further: its line is its share of the 250 GB GeoNode month, so size its pool or interval to that rate and never write a coded cap (c239). The p8 re-read rows cost far more than the plan; fix a re-read miss only inside the census share and leave the gap to Crawler guy, who takes it to the owner. The census Postgres writer row: its line names the worst slot; read the census writer lane's process count (crawler_v3_runtime_role_processes{role="instagram-census-writer"}) and the lane scaler's last pass (crawler_v3_lane_scaler_last_pass_timestamp_seconds), then fix the writer or its scaler through the crawler ops train, never by holding the census rate down. ig_queues_growing_6h: name the queue and its consumer from the backlog line and fix the consumer. crawler_panels_blank: the dashboards line names each blank panel; fix its query in auto-sns-agent apps/infra/grafana/dashboards/crawler or the exporter it reads, or delete a panel nobody needs, and land it through the crawler ops train. lane_gb_jumps: each gb_jump line names the lane or caller, its GB, its median and its top operations. Trace the jump the same day to the workload that makes it: for a lane, sum crawler.proxy_wire_reads wire_bytes by operation and hour over the 24 h and count otel.otel_traces root spans by SpanAttributes['http.request.header.x_virev_caller'] (`ops/bin/ch-ro` in auto-sns-agent) to name the caller or the scheduler setting behind it (an /ops/controls value such as throttle.watch_claims_per_tick or instagram_census.backlog_front_per_minute, a cadence such as a Watchlist's days, a backfill or a paid burst); for a caller, read product.usage_events by org, action, operation and api_key_id, and map an org to its owner (org_duty_parity_* are agent duties, org_virev_gtm_outreach is CRM developer VP, org_3* are customers). Then fix the cause the same day: a crawler setting or code path through /ops/controls with a measured reason or the crawler ops train, and a sibling's caller by a message to its owner with the GB and what to slow; size the work, never a coded cap (c239). A customer's or an agreed plan's growth, such as CRM's 3 GB a day plan 74502c590a, needs no fix and is named once with its GB against that plan. Every run with a jump, send Search product, misc. (d4's owner, GeoNode month) the lane or caller, its GB in 24 h, its median, the cause and the fix. A failed lane or caller read is a source_error: fix the read first. A source_error comes first: fix the precheck read. The duty job itself only reads prod. All on target: end the turn with no message.
